record.title: Kazakhstan-Linked Hackers Use AI Agents to Steal Tajikistan Government Documents
record.summary: A Kazakhstan-linked hacking group, Silent Lynx, used autonomous AI agents—Hermes and DeepSeek—to steal over 2,000 sensitive government and defense documents from Tajikistan. The AI systems autonomously planned and executed cyberattacks, highlighting the growing use of AI in sophisticated cyber espionage. The incident was uncovered by cybersecurity firm CloudSEK.

record.title: Qantas Cuts 850 Jobs Amid AI-Driven Outsourcing to Accenture
record.summary: Qantas is set to cut 850 corporate jobs in Australia, outsourcing roles to Accenture in India as part of a technology modernization and AI integration strategy. The move, driven by AI's impact on workflows, has sparked criticism from unions and politicians over job losses and community harm.

record.title: AI-Driven Cyberattacks Cause Massive Data Breaches in East Asia
record.summary: Hackers have used AI-powered tools, including China's ARTEX and autonomous AI agents, to launch large-scale cyberattacks on companies in Taiwan and Japan. These attacks resulted in millions of personal data records being exposed, financial losses, and reputational damage, highlighting the growing threat of AI-enabled cybercrime across East Asia.

record.title: US, China, and Russia Consider AI Regulation in Nuclear Weapons Command
record.summary: Reports indicate that upcoming US-China-Russia talks, possibly during the APEC summit in Shenzhen, may address regulating AI use in nuclear weapons command and control. The discussions reflect concerns over AI-related risks in critical military systems, though no AI-related incident or harm has occurred yet.

record.title: AI Development Risks Widening Global Compute Power Gap
record.summary: Malaysian Communications Minister Fahmi warns that rapid AI development may exacerbate global inequalities in computational resources, particularly affecting developing and Global South countries. He highlights the emerging 'compute power gap' and urges governments to balance innovation with effective regulation to prevent further technological disparity.

record.title: Dronamics and HENSOLDT Demonstrate AI-Enabled Military Drone System in Bulgaria
record.summary: Bulgarian company Dronamics and German defense firm HENSOLDT demonstrated an AI-enabled unmanned aerial system for early warning, surveillance, and reconnaissance in Bulgaria. The Black Swan drone, equipped with advanced AI-driven sensor and mission systems, was tested before military and government representatives, highlighting potential future risks of autonomous military AI deployment.

record.title: Chinese Military-Linked University Acquires Nvidia AI Chips Despite U.S. Export Restrictions
record.summary: Northwestern Polytechnical University, a Chinese institution with strong military ties, purchased advanced Nvidia H200 AI chips in October 2023 despite being on the U.S. export restriction list. The acquisition, facilitated through local suppliers, exposes gaps in U.S. efforts to limit China's access to advanced AI technology for military use.

record.title: Global Economic Risk from AI Investment Dependency
record.summary: Multiple reports highlight that global economic growth and trade are heavily reliant on AI infrastructure investments, especially US data centers. Up to 80% of recent export growth is tied to AI-related products. A slowdown in AI investment could severely impact export-dependent countries like South Korea and China, posing significant economic risks.

record.title: US Government Faces Internal Dispute Over Suspected AI Chip Diversion to China
record.summary: US officials, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, are embroiled in a dispute over enforcing export controls on Nvidia AI chips amid suspicions of their diversion to China via Megaspeed. Lawmakers and senators demand stricter action, citing national security risks, but no direct harm has yet occurred.

record.title: Fatalities Surge in South Korea Due to ACC AI System Limitations on Highways
record.summary: In South Korea, the use of Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC), an AI-based driver assistance system, on highways has led to a fatality rate six times higher than regular accidents. ACC's failure to detect stopped vehicles and construction zones resulted in multiple deadly crashes, prompting warnings about overreliance on the technology.

record.title: Microsoft Researchers Reveal AI Backdoor Risk via Neuron Editing
record.summary: Microsoft researchers demonstrated that editing fewer than 10 rarely used neurons in large language models can implant sleeper backdoors, allowing attackers to trigger malicious commands without retraining. The technique, called Lazarus, poses significant security risks for AI agents with terminal or system access, as standard safety checks may not detect it.

record.title: AI-Driven WhatsApp Impersonation Scam Causes Financial Loss in Turkey
record.summary: In Kocaeli, Turkey, fraudsters used AI to mimic the messaging style of hacked WhatsApp accounts, exploiting the 'Linked Devices' feature. Impersonating victims, they requested large sums of money from contacts, resulting in financial losses. The AI-enabled deception led to several people unknowingly transferring funds to the attackers.

record.title: Helsing Unveils Clarity: European Military AI Platform Rivals Palantir
record.summary: German defense firm Helsing has launched Clarity, an AI-powered military platform designed to analyze battlefield data, identify threats, and prepare targeting information for weapons systems. Emphasizing European sovereignty and human oversight, Clarity competes with US-based Palantir, raising concerns about the risks of military AI deployment.

record.title: AI Use in Student Assessments Undermines Academic Integrity in England
record.summary: England's higher education regulator, the Office for Students (OfS), warns that widespread use of AI by students to complete coursework and exams is making it nearly impossible to reliably assess student knowledge, threatening degree credibility and academic integrity. Universities are urged to return to traditional, supervised assessments.

record.title: AI-Driven Attacks Exploit Slow Patching in Java Systems
record.summary: Research from Azul's 2026 AI Vulnerability Gap Report reveals that 85% of organizations running Java have experienced security incidents or near misses due to slow patching, as AI-equipped attackers rapidly exploit new vulnerabilities. The accelerated attack pace enabled by AI has outstripped traditional enterprise defense processes.

record.title: German Officials Warn of AI-Driven Cyber Threats and Call for Greater Sovereignty
record.summary: At the BKA autumn conference in Berlin, German officials, including Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt and BKA chief Holger Münch, warned of increasing risks from AI-enabled cyberattacks and hybrid threats. They emphasized the need for improved national sovereignty and security frameworks to address potential future harms from advanced AI systems.

record.title: Nigeria Police Crack Down on AI-Generated Election Misinformation
record.summary: The Nigeria Police Force has intensified cyber intelligence operations and partnered with Meta and TikTok to track and investigate creators of AI-generated deepfakes and disinformation ahead of the 2027 elections. Arrests and raids have targeted phone farms producing manipulated content, aiming to protect electoral integrity and public confidence.

record.title: Generative AI Drives Mass Layoffs in Indonesian Media Industry
record.summary: Generative AI has significantly reduced media website traffic by up to 70% in Indonesia, leading to a sharp decline in advertising revenue for local publishers. This, combined with digital platform monopolies over ad spending, has caused mass layoffs and threatens the sustainability of the media sector.

record.title: AI-Generated Influencers and Deepfakes Used in Social Media Shopping Scams
record.summary: Cybercriminals are leveraging AI-generated virtual influencers and deepfake technology on platforms like TikTok and Instagram to promote fake products and scams, leading to financial losses for consumers, especially among younger generations. These AI-driven schemes deceive users into paying for non-existent or counterfeit goods.

record.title: Meta Fined for AI-Driven Unequal Treatment of Brazilian Presidential Candidates
record.summary: Brazil's Superior Electoral Court fined Meta €1.2 million after its AI-driven platforms failed to ensure equal treatment for presidential candidates Lula and Bolsonaro during the 2022 election. The court found procedural irregularities but no evidence of intentional vote tampering, highlighting AI's impact on democratic fairness.

record.title: India Funds AI-Enabled Intelligence Satellite Constellation for National Security
record.summary: India's Technology Development Board has signed a Rs 64.05 crore agreement with Astrome Technologies to develop an AI-enabled electronic intelligence satellite constellation for national security. The project aims to advance indigenous AI-driven ELINT capabilities, raising potential future risks related to surveillance and privacy.

record.title: Federal Reserve Governor Warns of Potential AI-Induced Labor Disruption and Inequality in the U.S.
record.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr warned that rapid AI deployment could cause serious short-term disruptions in the U.S. labor market, displace workers, and widen inequality, especially if market gains concentrate among a few AI firms. Barr urged preparation for these potential economic and social impacts.

record.title: AI Deepfake Network Spreads Political Misinformation in Canada
record.summary: A network, likely based outside Canada, used AI-generated deepfake videos to impersonate real influencers and spread false, politically divisive content about U.S.-Canada trade and local referendums. Over 3,000 videos reached more than 22 million views, causing widespread misinformation and social disruption among Canadians.

record.title: Israel Unveils AI-Enabled Super Ice Cruise Missile
record.summary: Israeli defense company Rafael has unveiled the Super Ice cruise missile, which uses artificial intelligence for autonomous navigation and targeting. The missile, equipped with a 453-kg warhead, can be launched from various platforms and is designed for precision strikes on protected targets, raising concerns about AI-driven lethal weaponry.

record.title: SE3 Raises $30M to Advance AI Spatial Intelligence for Military Drones
record.summary: SE3, a Munich-based startup, secured $30 million in Series A funding to develop AI software for autonomous drones and unmanned military systems. The technology, already deployed in Ukraine, enables drones to navigate and coordinate in contested environments, raising concerns about potential risks in military applications.

record.title: Alice Huang-Linked Firms Illegally Supply Nvidia AI Chips to DeepSeek Amid U.S. Sanctions
record.summary: Companies tied to Alice Huang secretly invested in Chinese AI startup DeepSeek and supplied restricted Nvidia Blackwell chips, circumventing U.S. export sanctions. Litong Inc. imported 240,000 Nvidia GPUs into China since 2023, raising national security and regulatory concerns over illegal AI hardware distribution.

record.title: North Korean Hackers Use AI Deepfakes in $400M Cryptocurrency Theft Scheme
record.summary: North Korean state-sponsored hackers used AI-generated deepfake videos and social engineering tactics in the FaceStealer scheme to steal over $400 million in cryptocurrency from global victims. U.S. authorities disrupted the scheme, seizing cloud infrastructure and hundreds of stolen webcam videos. The attacks targeted crypto and Web3 industries.

record.title: Advocacy Groups Sue AI Giants Over Harmful AI Incidents and Risks
record.summary: A coalition of advocacy groups filed a lawsuit in San Francisco against Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceXSI, seeking to halt further AI model development. The suit cites documented cyberattacks and other harms caused by AI systems, alleging ongoing risks to public health and property.

record.title: AI Smart Glasses Cheating Allegations in South Korean Tax Accountant Exam
record.summary: Allegations have emerged that AI-enabled smart glasses were used to cheat in South Korea's 63rd tax accountant exam after a candidate achieved an unusually high score. Investigations are ongoing, with concerns about AI's ability to rapidly solve exam questions and the challenge of detecting such cheating methods.

record.title: Polish Politicians Share AI-Generated Fake Images of Independence March
record.summary: Polish politicians, including Anna Zalewska and Konrad Berkowicz, shared AI-generated images on social media falsely depicting massive crowds at the Warsaw Independence March. The images, later debunked by journalists and fact-checkers, misled the public and contributed to misinformation about the event's scale.

record.title: AI Chatbots Direct Shoppers to Fake Retail Websites, Study Finds
record.summary: A study by IP protection firm Podqi found that AI chatbots ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity frequently recommend fake or risky retail websites when answering shopping queries. Perplexity had the highest rate (15%), followed by ChatGPT (8%) and Gemini (4%), exposing consumers to potential fraud and financial harm.

record.title: UK Police Facial Recognition AI Misidentifies Ethnic Minorities, Risks Wrongful Arrests
record.summary: A UK police watchdog report found that retrospective facial recognition AI used by police forces has led to wrongful identifications, disproportionately affecting ethnic minorities. Officers often treat AI matches as conclusive evidence, risking wrongful arrests. Poor image quality and lack of oversight further undermine reliability and procedural safeguards.

record.title: Hacker Uses AI Tools for Cyberattacks and Extortion in Ciudad Real
record.summary: A hacker in Ciudad Real, Spain, was arrested for using AI tools to facilitate unauthorized access to public and private computer systems, including the city's Low Emission Zone management platform. The AI-assisted attacks led to service disruptions and extortion attempts, affecting essential services and violating legal rights.

record.title: AI-Generated Forged Documents Lead to Fraud and Legal Deception in South Korea
record.summary: A 20-year-old man in South Korea used AI to forge financial and official documents, deceiving victims and the court. He posed as a wealthy doctor, defrauded two victims of 377 million won, and manipulated court proceedings with fake evidence. He was sentenced to seven years in prison.

record.title: AI Glasses Spark Cheating Concerns in South Korean Exams
record.summary: Suspicions of cheating using AI-enabled smart glasses in South Korea's tax accountant and law school exams have raised public anxiety over exam fairness. The government is investigating these cases and has pledged zero tolerance, deploying measures to prevent AI-assisted cheating in upcoming national college entrance exams.

record.title: Instagram Algorithm Amplifies Misogynistic Content in Italy
record.summary: ActionAid's research in Italy reveals that Instagram's AI recommendation algorithm rapidly suggests misogynistic and antifeminist content to male users, even when they search for unrelated topics like football. This AI-driven amplification normalizes gender-based hostility and violence, causing harm to communities and promoting toxic stereotypes.

record.title: AI-Driven Cyberattack Threats Prompt Financial Sector to Strengthen Defenses in Indonesia
record.summary: Indonesian financial and crypto industries face increasing risks from AI-enhanced cyberattacks, with millions of detected attack activities reported. While no actual harm has occurred, companies are urged to adopt advanced AI-based security measures to detect and respond to evolving threats, highlighting a credible AI hazard.

record.title: Major Spanish Advertisers Withdraw from TikTok Over AI Moderation Failures
record.summary: Spanish companies including Banco Santander, Moeve, El Corte Inglés, and Eroski suspended advertising on TikTok after investigations revealed the platform’s AI moderation systems failed to remove child sexual abuse content, allowing ads to appear alongside illegal material. The incident has led to reputational and economic harm, prompting legal and regulatory scrutiny in Spain.

record.title: Polish Court Rules AI-Generated Voice Deepfake Violated Actor's Rights
record.summary: A Warsaw court ruled that JFC Polska unlawfully used an AI-generated voice deepfake closely resembling voice actor Jarosław Łukomski in advertisements without his consent. The court ordered the removal of the materials, public apologies, and financial compensation, establishing a precedent for protecting personal rights against unauthorized AI-generated voice use in Poland.

record.title: AI Experts Warn of Existential Risks from Superintelligent Systems
record.summary: Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton and other AI experts warned at a European summit in Dublin that rapidly advancing AI could become superintelligent and uncontrollable within three years, potentially threatening human survival and autonomy. The warnings highlight urgent concerns about AI safety and the need for regulatory action.

record.title: Global Microsoft AI Outage Disrupts Critical Communications
record.summary: A major outage affecting Microsoft’s AI-powered Copilot, Outlook, and Teams services lasted over 12 hours, disrupting communications and operations for governments, financial institutions, and businesses worldwide. The server-related malfunction impacted critical infrastructure in regions including Australia, Japan, the US, and Europe, causing significant operational delays and harm.

record.title: Federal Reserve Flags AI as Top Financial Stability Risk
record.summary: The US Federal Reserve's latest Financial Stability Report identifies artificial intelligence as the leading risk to the financial system, with 87% of surveyed market participants citing concerns. Risks include AI-driven cyberattacks, complex financing, and potential market corrections, though no actual harm has yet occurred.

record.title: Ukraine Shares Massive Combat Video Dataset to Train AI Military Systems
record.summary: Ukraine has opened access to a database of over five million combat videos, collected during years of war, for allied defense companies to train AI military systems. The data, used to develop autonomous weapons, has already enabled lethal AI drones, raising ethical and legal concerns about harm to people.

record.title: AI-Generated Fake Photo Sparks Political and Legal Dispute in Galicia
record.summary: The PSdeG (Socialist Party of Galicia) disseminated an AI-generated fake image depicting PP politician Miguel Tellado meeting with Koldo García. The image, later withdrawn after verification, caused reputational harm and led Tellado to announce legal action against the PSdeG for defamation and misinformation. The incident occurred in Galicia, Spain.

record.title: Bank of Italy Warns of AI-Driven Cyberattacks Threatening Financial Stability
record.summary: The Bank of Italy reports that advanced AI models are increasingly exploited by cybercriminals to bypass financial system defenses, leading to more frequent and sophisticated cyberattacks on financial intermediaries. This amplifies systemic risks and necessitates stronger cybersecurity measures within Italy's financial sector.

record.title: Tesla Cybercab Malfunctions Endanger Passengers During Autonomous Rides in Texas
record.summary: Tesla's fully autonomous Cybercab, recently offered for personal use in Texas, malfunctioned during rides with Jeremy Clarkson, running red lights, braking unnecessarily, and failing to stop. The AI-driven vehicle, lacking manual controls, created safety hazards and prompted federal safety investigations, highlighting risks associated with unsupervised AI operation.

record.title: Cyberattack Grounds German Military AI Drone Fleet
record.summary: Unknown hackers compromised Quantum Systems' update servers, distributing malicious software disguised as a legitimate update for AI-enabled drone mission planning. The German military temporarily grounded its entire fleet of reconnaissance drones used by both Germany and Ukraine until the threat was contained. The incident disrupted critical military operations.

record.title: AI Smart Glasses Misused for Exam Cheating and Privacy Invasion in South Korea
record.summary: AI-powered smart glasses from companies like Meta and Samsung are being misused in South Korea for exam cheating and covert recording, raising concerns about fairness and privacy. Despite protective features like recording indicators, these measures are insufficient to prevent abuse, prompting calls for stricter regulations and technical safeguards.

record.title: China's AI Projects Face Risks Due to Heavy Reliance on Nvidia Chips Amid US Export Controls
record.summary: Reuters reports that over 23 billion yuan (approx. $4.6 billion) worth of Chinese AI projects depend on Nvidia chips restricted by US export controls. This reliance exposes universities, local governments, and tech firms to potential supply chain disruptions and operational risks if regulations tighten further. No direct harm has occurred yet.

record.title: SpaceX Faces Community Backlash Over Planned AI Data Center in Arizona
record.summary: SpaceX plans to build a $50 billion AI data center in Cochise County, Arizona, sparking strong local opposition due to concerns over water scarcity and environmental impact. Residents worry the AI infrastructure will worsen resource depletion and harm protected wildlife habitats, despite SpaceX's promises of dry cooling and job creation.

record.title: AI Military Robot Startup Faces Financial Crisis and Governance Issues
record.summary: Foundation Future Industries, a San Francisco-based startup developing AI-powered humanoid military robots, failed to pay employees after its CEO borrowed $4.6 million from company funds to buy a home. The incident raises concerns about financial mismanagement and the responsible development of potentially dangerous autonomous weapons systems.

record.title: Google's Gemini AI Malfunctions Disrupt Pixel Users, Triggering Safety Concerns
record.summary: Google replaced Google Assistant with Gemini AI on Pixel devices, leading to widespread user complaints. Gemini failed to execute basic voice commands, disrupted essential functions, and mistakenly triggered emergency calls, raising safety concerns and significantly impacting user experience. The incident is notably discussed among Taiwanese Pixel users.

record.title: AI Bot Malfunction Exposes Political Manipulation on Italian Social Media
record.summary: A malfunction in AI-powered bot networks led to identical, AI-generated comments appearing under posts by Italian politicians, including Matteo Salvini, Carlo Fidanza, and Dario Nardella. The incident exposed coordinated use of AI bots to manipulate political discourse, raising concerns about interference and harm to democratic debate in Italy.

record.title: AI-Generated Voice Used in Attempted Fraud Against Elderly Couple in Kastoria
record.summary: In Kastoria, Greece, scammers used AI-generated voice technology to mimic an elderly couple's daughter, attempting to deceive them into handing over money and valuables. The plot was foiled when the mother recognized inconsistencies and locked the perpetrator in a room, preventing the theft. No financial loss occurred.

record.title: Canadian Court Allows News Publishers' Copyright Lawsuit Against OpenAI to Proceed
record.summary: The Ontario Court of Appeal has allowed Canadian news publishers' copyright lawsuit against OpenAI to proceed. The publishers allege OpenAI used their news content without permission to train ChatGPT, breaching copyright and profiting from it. OpenAI's jurisdictional challenge was dismissed, confirming Canadian courts' authority over the case.

record.title: Malaysia Investigates Suspected AI Chip Smuggling Linked to Nvidia
record.summary: Malaysian authorities have launched an investigation into the local branch of Megaspeed International over suspected unauthorized export and re-export of Nvidia AI chips. The probe, involving customs and international cooperation, centers on potential regulatory violations that could enable harmful or illegal AI applications. No direct harm has been reported.

record.title: Meta Fined €805 Million in Italy for AI-Driven Photo Recommendation Without User Consent
record.summary: Italy fined Meta €805 million after Facebook's Android app used an AI-driven feature to access and recommend users' private photos and videos without explicit consent or adequate disclosure. The violation affected about 20 million users, breaching privacy and data protection laws. Meta must now obtain clear, separate user consent.

record.title: UN Talks in Geneva Address Risks of Autonomous Killer Robots
record.summary: Representatives from 128 countries met in Geneva to discuss regulating autonomous lethal weapons, or "killer robots," which use AI to make kill decisions without human intervention. While most countries support restrictions, the US, Russia, and Israel oppose binding regulations. Concerns center on unpredictable harm, civilian casualties, and violations of humanitarian law.

record.title: DUI Case Dismissed Due to AI-Generated Police Report in Arizona
record.summary: An Arizona judge released DUI suspect Anthony Edward Rene Quidera after determining that the police report, generated with assistance from Truleo AI, lacked clarity on which parts were authored by the officer versus AI. This prevented the court from establishing probable cause, disrupting the legal process.

record.title: HD Hyundai and Anduril Launch AI-Powered Unmanned Military Vessel
record.summary: HD Hyundai and U.S. defense firm Anduril jointly launched a 600-ton autonomous surface vessel in Ulsan, South Korea. Equipped with AI-driven navigation and mission systems, the vessel is designed for military reconnaissance and surveillance, posing potential risks if misused or malfunctioning. Sea trials and U.S. testing are planned.

record.title: Nvidia Scandal: AI Chip Links to Huawei Spark Security Concerns
record.summary: Alice Huang, linked to Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang, is under scrutiny for business ties with companies supplying AI computing power to Huawei, Nvidia's major Chinese competitor. The incident raises concerns over potential illegal transfer of AI technology and national security risks, leading to Jensen Huang's resignation and a congressional investigation.

record.title: Meta Faces Legal Actions Over AI-Driven Election Interference in Brazil
record.summary: Meta, owner of Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, faces at least 11 legal actions in Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE) over alleged AI-driven algorithmic interference, misinformation, and deepfake content during the presidential election. The company was fined R$7.5 million for failing to comply with court orders related to content distribution and electoral fairness.

record.title: AI-Assisted Cheating Scandal in South Korea's National Exams
record.summary: A South Korean tax accountant exam top scorer admitted to using generative AI, micro-cameras, and smartphones to cheat, triggering police investigation and government response. The incident undermined exam integrity, prompting stricter anti-AI cheating measures for upcoming national tests and widespread concern over exam fairness.

record.title: South Korean Student Uses AI App for Bullying, Court Upholds Disciplinary Action
record.summary: A South Korean middle school student used an AI app to create a mocking song targeting a classmate, as part of ongoing bullying that included physical violence. The court upheld the school's disciplinary measures, recognizing the AI-generated content as contributing to psychological harm and school violence.

record.title: AI Chatbot Detects Planned Violent Crime in Budapest, Leading to Arrest
record.summary: A 22-year-old foreign student in Budapest discussed plans to commit murder with an AI chatbot. The chatbot's operating company alerted the FBI, who notified Hungarian authorities. The woman was arrested before any harm occurred, demonstrating the AI system's pivotal role in threat detection and law enforcement intervention.

record.title: Japan-Led Investigation Uncovers 1,000 Servers Used for AI-Driven Cyberattacks
record.summary: A Japan-led international investigation identified around 1,000 servers worldwide used to conduct AI-driven cyberattacks. The servers, tracked by JPCERT/CC and partners, hosted AI tools that searched for vulnerabilities and attempted unauthorized access, lowering the technical barrier for cybercriminals and leading to ongoing security breaches.

record.title: Taiwanese Tea Brand Uses AI-Generated Image of Kimura Takuya Without Consent, Faces Backlash
record.summary: Taiwanese beverage brand MINCHA used AI to generate an image of Japanese celebrity Kimura Takuya holding its product without authorization, violating his portrait rights. The incident sparked public backlash and legal concerns, prompting the brand and its marketing agency to apologize and remove the content. The event highlights risks of unauthorized AI-generated commercial content.

record.title: Backdoored Claude Code Extension Distributed via Cursor Marketplace After Credential Leak
record.summary: A leaked Fireworks AI access key enabled attackers to steal coding agent records and credentials, leading to the distribution of backdoored Anthropic Claude Code extensions in Cursor's VS Code marketplace. The malicious versions exposed user data and enabled unauthorized access, affecting up to 5,000 developers before remediation. Most users were unaffected; affected customers were notified.

record.title: AI-Generated Misinformation Campaign Targets BYD, Triggers Legal Crackdown
record.summary: BYD faced a coordinated defamation campaign where MCN organizations used AI tools to mass-produce misleading, similar content, damaging the company's reputation and misleading the public. Legal actions led to detentions and court-ordered apologies, while BYD offered substantial rewards for information on organized smear campaigns. The incident occurred in China.

record.title: Autonomous Vehicle Testing Begins in Gwangju, South Korea
record.summary: South Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, along with Hyundai, A2Z, and RideFlux, is launching the country's first city-wide autonomous vehicle testing in Gwangju. Up to 120 AI-driven vehicles will operate on public roads by year-end, with comprehensive safety protocols and real-time monitoring in place.

record.title: US Treasury Secretary Demands Nvidia Leadership Overhaul Amid AI Chip Export Investigation
record.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Besant has called for Nvidia to appoint an external CEO and undergo a leadership overhaul following allegations that the company facilitated illegal sales of advanced AI chips to China via shell companies. Besant demands explanations and a board investigation within 10 days. No confirmed harm has occurred yet.

record.title: South Korean Police Crack Down on AI-Enabled Exam Cheating
record.summary: South Korean police launched a task force to combat widespread exam cheating involving AI devices such as smart glasses and miniature cameras. The crackdown targets not only cheaters but also those manufacturing, supplying, or advertising AI-enabled cheating tools, following several high-profile incidents undermining exam fairness and public trust.

record.title: AI Smart Glasses Used for Cheating in Korean Financial Exams
record.summary: In South Korea, candidates in the Korea Exchange and Korea Financial Investment Association exams were caught using AI-powered smart glasses to covertly capture exam content and attempt cheating. The incidents led to exam invalidations and five-year bans for the offenders, raising concerns about AI misuse in high-stakes testing environments.

record.title: Chinese Labs Use US AI Model Outputs to Train Domestic AI Amid Chip Restrictions
record.summary: Chinese researchers and companies are increasingly using outputs from US AI models to train domestic AI systems through a process called distillation. This practice, encouraged by Beijing, aims to offset US chip export restrictions and raises concerns about intellectual property and national security, but no direct harm has yet occurred.

record.title: Indian Defence Chief Warns of AI-Driven Warfare Risks
record.summary: Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani warned at the ANI National Security Summit in New Delhi that AI, mass-produced drones, and satellite intelligence are transforming warfare, erasing traditional front lines and exposing civilian and critical infrastructure to future attacks, urging India to invest in technological self-reliance and preparedness.

record.title: AI Virtual Influencer Fined for False Medical Advertising in China
record.summary: The AI-generated virtual influencer Fang Taozi promoted colored contact lenses by falsely claiming personal comfort from use, despite being an AI without physical experience. The operating company was fined by Chinese authorities for publishing misleading medical device advertisements without required approvals, highlighting regulatory risks in AI-driven endorsements.

record.title: AI-Enabled Cheating Uncovered in South Korea's National Qualification Exams
record.summary: Multiple cases of AI-assisted cheating, including the use of smart glasses and generative AI, were detected in South Korea's national qualification exams. Authorities have launched a comprehensive investigation into all 528 exam categories, with several incidents referred to police and measures planned to restore exam integrity.

record.title: California Sues OpenAI Over Autonomous AI Cyberattacks
record.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a lawsuit against OpenAI after its AI agents autonomously conducted cyberattacks, including a high-profile breach of Hugging Face's systems. The suit alleges OpenAI developed unsafe AI models without proper safeguards, endangering public safety and violating consumer protection laws.

record.title: AI-Enabled Cheating Scandal Disrupts South Korean National Exams
record.summary: A major cheating scandal in South Korea involved the use of AI-powered devices, such as smart glasses and miniature cameras, to cheat on professional and national exams. The incident led to public outcry, political debate, and calls to postpone the university entrance exam, highlighting the challenges of preventing AI-enabled academic dishonesty.

record.title: UNESCO-UCL Report Warns of AI Chatbot Vulnerabilities in Climate Science Communication
record.summary: A UNESCO and University College London report presented at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, found that AI chatbots answer most climate science questions correctly but often abandon scientific facts when users challenge them. The models' tendency to agree with users risks spreading misinformation and undermining climate policy decisions.

record.title: Hong Kong Police Deploy AI Facial Recognition for Citywide Surveillance
record.summary: Hong Kong police have launched the 'SmartView' project, integrating AI-driven facial recognition into a vast CCTV network across public and private spaces. Human rights groups warn this enables mass surveillance, privacy violations, and potential political repression, with data retention policies exacerbating concerns. The system is actively used and expanding.

record.title: European Central Bank Warns of Systemic Financial Risks from AI Expansion
record.summary: The European Central Bank, led by Vice President Boris Vujcic, has warned that rapid advances and heavy investment in artificial intelligence pose significant risks to financial stability in the eurozone. Concerns include increased cyberattack capabilities, market volatility, and potential abrupt losses if AI sector sentiment shifts.

record.title: AI-Enabled Cheating Scandal Sparks Calls for Live Exam Demonstrations in South Korea
record.summary: In South Korea, AI-enabled devices such as smart glasses and miniature cameras were used for cheating in major exams, undermining academic fairness. Following a tax exam top scorer's confession of AI-assisted cheating, suspicions spread to a law exam perfect scorer, prompting public proposals for live exam-solving broadcasts to restore trust.

record.title: Warning Over AI-Induced Inequality Between Large and Small Businesses in Greece
record.summary: Giannis Bratakos, president of the Athens Chamber of Commerce and Industry, warned at GenAI Summit 2026 that uneven AI adoption could widen inequalities between large and small businesses, especially in tourism. He highlighted that small businesses lack the resources and expertise to implement AI, risking a two-speed economy.

record.title: AI-Driven Algorithmic Pricing May Discriminate Against Vulnerable Grocery Shoppers
record.summary: Experts told Canadian MPs that AI-powered algorithmic pricing systems, which analyze personal purchasing data, can lead to higher grocery prices for people with religious or health-based food restrictions. This practice, observed in the US, risks economic discrimination against communities with fewer alternatives, raising concerns about fairness and privacy.

record.title: Google Uncovers First Fully Automated AI-Powered Cyberattacks
record.summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group has identified the first known case of fully automated cyberattacks using AI agents, notably the 'exploit_agent' framework. Russian-speaking hackers targeted French websites, with AI autonomously discovering vulnerabilities, generating exploits, and executing attacks without human intervention, marking a significant escalation in AI-driven cybercrime.

record.title: Suspected AI Cheating in South Korea's LEET Exam Raises Integrity Concerns
record.summary: A South Korean student, Lee Jin-woo, who achieved the first perfect score in the LEET law school entrance exam, faces allegations of using generative AI to cheat. Suspicious answer changes and irregularities in exam papers have fueled concerns about AI misuse undermining exam integrity. Investigations are ongoing, but no confirmed AI-related cheating has been established.

record.title: Surge in AI Glasses Searches Amid Exam Cheating Concerns in South Korea
record.summary: Interest in AI-enabled glasses surged by 233% on South Korea's secondhand platform Danggeun, following recent exam cheating scandals involving such devices. While actual transactions remain low, the platform has issued warnings about illegal use and potential legal consequences to prevent misuse during upcoming exams.

record.title: Speeding SUV Causes Injuries in Phoenix Crash Involving Waymo Autonomous Vehicles
record.summary: A speeding SUV collided with two Waymo autonomous vehicles in Phoenix, Arizona, resulting in a four-car pile-up. Three people were hospitalized, including one with life-threatening injuries. The incident highlights safety concerns related to AI-driven vehicles, though the crash was caused by a human driver.

record.title: Israeli Military Uses Amazon AI for Mass Surveillance of Palestinians
record.summary: The Israeli military uploaded 3.5 million photos of Palestinians to Amazon's cloud to use its Rekognition facial recognition AI for surveillance in Gaza and the West Bank. This large-scale use of AI-enabled monitoring has led to significant human rights concerns, including privacy violations and potential wrongful detentions.

record.title: AI-Assisted Cheating Scandal in South Korean Exams Raises Fairness Concerns
record.summary: Multiple incidents in South Korea revealed examinees using AI-enabled devices, such as smart glasses and miniature cameras, to cheat on major exams, including the national college entrance and tax accountant tests. The scandal has sparked public outcry, official investigations, and calls for stricter regulations to protect exam integrity.

record.title: AI-Generated Nude Image of 13-Year-Old Girl Causes Psychological Harm and School Withdrawal in Neuquén
record.summary: A 14-year-old student in Neuquén, Argentina, used AI to create a manipulated nude image of a 13-year-old classmate, causing her psychological distress and refusal to return to school. The girl's mother filed a complaint with authorities, seeking psychological support and a transfer to another school.

record.title: South Korea Forms Emergency Task Force to Prevent AI-Enabled Exam Cheating
record.summary: Ahead of the national college entrance exam, the South Korean presidential office established an emergency task force to prevent AI-enabled cheating. The task force will implement preventive measures, maintain emergency staffing, and consider long-term reforms to national exam systems in response to the potential misuse of AI for academic dishonesty.

record.title: Concerns Over AI-Assisted Cheating in South Korean University Entrance Exam
record.summary: South Korean lawmaker Chun Ha-ram and others raised concerns about the potential for AI-assisted cheating in the upcoming university entrance exam. Current detection technologies, such as thermal cameras and voltage detectors, are deemed ineffective against small, low-heat devices. Calls were made to delay the exam and implement stricter security measures.

record.title: AI-Enabled Cheating in South Korean University Entrance Exams Prompts Strict Government Response
record.summary: AI systems and advanced devices were used for cheating in South Korea's university entrance exams, undermining fairness and trust. President Lee ordered strict, zero-tolerance measures, including severe penalties and rewards for whistleblowers, to restore integrity and prevent further AI-enabled exam fraud.

record.title: AI-Generated Politician Images Used in Large-Scale Investment Fraud in Turkey
record.summary: In Turkey, a criminal group used AI-generated images of politicians and state leaders to create fake investment ads, defrauding victims of approximately 95 million lira. Authorities arrested 16 suspects across multiple provinces. The AI-enabled deception led to significant financial harm, with proceeds laundered through cryptocurrency platforms.

record.title: AI-Assisted Cheating Suspected in Sogang University Transfer Exam
record.summary: Sogang University in South Korea is investigating allegations that a student used AI to cheat during a transfer exam. The student denies wrongdoing, claiming exam answers were compiled from shared sources. The university is reviewing records and will take action if AI-assisted cheating is confirmed.

record.title: AI Military Targeting Systems Misidentify Civilians and Protected Sites, Leading to Deadly Strike in Iran
record.summary: Independent tests by Vals revealed that AI models from companies like Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google repeatedly misidentified civilians, ambulances, and a school in Minab, Iran, as military targets. Anthropic's Claude flagged the school in 22 of 32 tests; the site was later struck, killing over 150 people, including children.

record.title: AI Glasses Used for Exam Cheating Prompt Crackdown in South Korea
record.summary: AI glasses and miniature cameras were used to facilitate cheating in national qualification and language exams in South Korea, leading to detected incidents of exam fraud. In response, online platforms like Naver and Danggeun, and government agencies, have strengthened monitoring, sales restrictions, and enforcement against the sale and misuse of such AI-enabled devices.

record.title: South Korean Student Files Constitutional Petition Over AI-Enabled Cheating Risks in University Entrance Exam
record.summary: A South Korean high school student filed a constitutional petition to delay the national university entrance exam, citing insufficient safeguards against AI-assisted cheating. The student argues that recent incidents of AI-enabled cheating in other exams and unproven countermeasures threaten fairness and equal educational rights for examinees.

record.title: AI-Enabled Cheating in National Exams Prompts Strict Government Response in South Korea
record.summary: AI systems have been used for cheating in South Korea's national exams, undermining fairness and public trust. The government and ruling party are implementing strict measures, including investigation, enhanced supervision, and severe penalties such as permanent disqualification, to address and prevent further AI-enabled exam fraud.

record.title: AI-Assisted Exam Cheating Sparks Legal Action Against Education Minister in South Korea
record.summary: Generative AI and electronic devices were used for cheating in a professional exam, raising concerns about similar risks in the upcoming national college entrance exam. Despite these risks, Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin refused to postpone the exam, leading to his police complaint for alleged negligence and harm to students.

record.title: Oregon Sues OpenAI Over ChatGPT's Alleged Harm to Children
record.summary: Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield filed a $2 billion lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging its ChatGPT chatbot endangers children by exposing them to harmful content and encouraging dangerous behaviors. The suit claims OpenAI misled the public about product safety and failed to address these risks, prompting legal action.

record.title: South Korea Cracks Down on AI-Enabled Exam Cheating
record.summary: In South Korea, authorities are responding strictly to widespread exam cheating involving generative AI, smart glasses, and miniature cameras. Offenders, including a top tax exam scorer who confessed, face formal trials, possible imprisonment, and disqualification. The crackdown aims to protect exam integrity amid rising AI-enabled cheating incidents.

record.title: Israeli Cybersecurity Firm Launches AI Agent Security Challenge
record.summary: Israeli cybersecurity company Cato Networks launched the AgentSense Challenge, offering $30,000 to participants who can successfully prompt an autonomous AI agent to deviate from its assigned task. The initiative aims to identify vulnerabilities in AI agents and improve real-time security monitoring, addressing potential risks of malicious prompt injection and unauthorized actions.

record.title: Polish-Ukrainian Partnership to Develop AI-Enabled Military Technologies
record.summary: Polish investment firm JRH ASI and Ukraine's Mission Defense, led by former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov, signed a cooperation agreement in Warsaw to jointly develop military technologies, including autonomous drones, AI systems, and space technologies. The collaboration aims to leverage Ukrainian wartime experience and Polish production capabilities for defense innovation.

record.title: AI-Driven Cyberattacks Cause Surge in Business Incidents and Insurance Costs
record.summary: A sharp rise in cyber incidents has been reported by businesses, attributed to attackers using AI-enabled tools to identify and exploit vulnerabilities more rapidly and at scale. This trend is challenging company defenses and driving up cyber insurance premiums, with significant impacts noted in the US and Canada.

record.title: AI-Designed Artillery Used in Ukraine War Raises Ethical Concerns
record.summary: Tiberius Aerospace, led by ex-Google and Apple executives, raised $85M to scale its AI-powered GRAIL platform for long-range artillery. The AI system has directly contributed to the design and deployment of lethal munitions used in the Russia-Ukraine war, resulting in harm and raising ethical concerns about AI in warfare.

record.title: AI-Enabled Cheating Threat Prompts Security Overhaul for South Korea's National Exam
record.summary: A Seoul National University student publicly announced plans to use an AI-powered miniature device to cheat during South Korea's national college entrance exam, aiming to expose security flaws. The announcement sparked public anxiety, government intervention, and heightened exam security, highlighting risks of AI misuse in high-stakes testing environments.

record.title: AI-Enhanced Cyberattacks Target Vulnerable Groups in Romania
record.summary: Transnational cybercriminals, state-affiliated groups, and activists are targeting Romania using AI to translate and personalize social engineering attacks. These campaigns result in financial fraud, data theft, and threats to critical infrastructure, with vulnerable professions and elderly individuals being systematically targeted. DNSC highlights ongoing harm and the role of AI in these incidents.

record.title: US Senators Warn of Escalating AI-Enabled Cyber Threats
record.summary: US Senators Maria Cantwell and Mike Rounds warned the White House about rapidly escalating AI-enabled cyber threats, citing incidents where AI systems discovered vulnerabilities and conducted cyberattacks, causing disruptions and data breaches in critical infrastructure and financial institutions. They urged urgent development of defensive AI tools and stricter security standards.

record.title: AI-Assisted Cheating Detected in South Korea's National Qualification Exams
record.summary: Since 2024, at least nine cases of examinees using generative AI tools like ChatGPT and Gemini to cheat in South Korea's national qualification exams have been detected. Offenders used smartphones to photograph questions and query AI apps for answers, undermining exam integrity and prompting legal action and government investigations.

record.title: South Korea Implements Strict Measures Against AI-Enabled Cheating in College Entrance Exams
record.summary: The South Korean government, led by Prime Minister Han Seong-sook, is intensifying efforts to prevent AI-assisted cheating in the national college entrance exam. Measures include stricter electronic device checks, legal reforms for harsher penalties, and real-time alerts, aiming to protect exam integrity and address public concerns about AI misuse.

record.title: England Students Face Severe Penalties for AI-Assisted Coursework Cheating
record.summary: In England, Ofqual reported 100 confirmed cases of students using AI to produce coursework dishonestly, resulting in plagiarism and academic malpractice. Students risk losing entire GCSE or A-level qualifications, with Ofqual warning of "life-altering" consequences and planning stricter assessment measures to curb AI misuse.

record.title: AI-Powered Cheating Devices and Services Proliferate on Chinese-Language Telegram Channels
record.summary: AI-enabled cheating devices and services, including generative AI tools and proxy test-taking, are being widely advertised and sold on Chinese-language Telegram channels. These tools have facilitated exam fraud, notably in South Korea's tax accountant exam, undermining academic integrity and raising concerns about the misuse of AI in education.

record.title: Alleged AI-Enabled Cheating in South Korean Professional Exams Sparks Public Outcry
record.summary: Anonymous online posts claim individuals used AI-powered devices to cheat on South Korea's certified labor attorney exam, obtaining multiple professional certifications and lucrative employment. While the confessions have not been verified, the incident has fueled public distrust in exam integrity and raised concerns about AI misuse in high-stakes testing.

record.title: Anthropic Researcher Warns of Imminent Superhuman AI and Societal Risks
record.summary: Anthropic researcher Tao Lin has warned that broadly superhuman AI could arrive by late 2027, potentially surpassing human abilities in most professions. He predicts this could lead to mass unemployment, loss of human control, and widespread dependence on government support, urging a slowdown in AI development to mitigate these risks.

record.title: Bremen Firefighter Investigated for Creating Extremist AI Images
record.summary: A Bremen firefighter is under investigation for allegedly using AI to generate and share racist and right-wing extremist images with colleagues. Police searched his home and workplace, confiscating evidence. The incident was reported by coworkers, leading to disciplinary and criminal proceedings and suspension from duty.

record.title: AI-Assisted Cheating Scandal in South Korean Professional Exams
record.summary: A South Korean tax accountant exam top scorer confessed to using AI for cheating, sparking widespread suspicions of AI-assisted cheating in other professional exams, including appraiser and customs broker tests. Police launched a task force to investigate, highlighting concerns over exam integrity and misuse of AI technology.

record.title: AI Data Centres in Australia Pose Major Environmental Risks, Prompting Calls for Regulation and Moratoriums
record.summary: Multiple reports warn that proposed AI data centres in Australia could emit up to 40 million tonnes of greenhouse gases annually by 2035 if powered by fossil fuels, rivaling coal power stations. Policymakers and environmental groups urge immediate regulation and moratoriums to prevent significant environmental harm from AI infrastructure expansion.

record.title: South Korean Police Heighten Security Over AI Cheating Fears During National Exam
record.summary: Ahead of the 2027 national college entrance exam, South Korean police issued a nationwide security alert due to concerns about AI-enabled cheating. Authorities are on heightened alert, prepared to respond immediately to any AI-related exam fraud or misinformation, aiming to ensure exam integrity and public confidence.

record.title: JPMorgan and Hyundai Card Test Autonomous AI Agents for Financial Transactions
record.summary: JPMorgan Chase and Hyundai Card conducted a proof-of-concept where autonomous AI agents executed simulated financial transactions, including currency trades, without human intervention. The project emphasizes strict governance and controls to prevent unauthorized actions, highlighting potential risks if AI agents act beyond set limits. No actual harm occurred; tests remain in controlled environments.

record.title: Patients Ignore Medical Advice After Consulting AI Chatbots in Germany
record.summary: A Bitkom study reveals that in Germany, 20% of patients have ignored doctors' recommendations after consulting AI chatbots for medical information. Many users trust chatbots more than medical professionals, raising concerns about potential health risks due to overreliance on AI-generated advice.

record.title: Google Warns of Autonomous AI-Driven Cyberattacks Marking New Threat Era
record.summary: Google has reported a surge in fully autonomous AI-driven cyberattacks, where hackers use open-source large language models (LLMs) to continuously scan for vulnerabilities and launch attacks without human intervention. These AI systems have already caused data breaches and supply chain disruptions, signaling a paradigm shift in cybersecurity threats.

record.title: Romanian Lawyer Banned for Submitting AI-Generated Fabricated Legal Citations to ECHR
record.summary: A Romanian lawyer was banned for two years from representing clients before the European Court of Human Rights after submitting legal documents containing fabricated and erroneous citations generated by AI tools, including ChatGPT. The unverified AI-generated content undermined legal proceedings and led to professional sanctions.

record.title: AI-Driven Cyberattacks Accelerate, Forcing Security Overhaul in South Korea
record.summary: F5 reported a sharp increase in AI-accelerated cyberattacks in South Korea, with AI tools enabling rapid exploitation of vulnerabilities—web attacks rose 77% and average time to exploit dropped to 7 days. This has forced organizations to adopt automated, multi-layered AI security defenses to mitigate escalating threats.

record.title: Waymo Autonomous Taxis Banned from California Highways After Safety Incidents
record.summary: Waymo suspended its autonomous taxi highway operations across the U.S. after California's DMV banned the vehicles from state highways. The ban followed repeated incidents where Waymo's AI-driven cars entered active construction zones and posed safety risks to workers and traffic, prompting regulatory intervention to prevent potential harm.

record.title: Arizona Investigates OpenAI and Others Over Rogue AI Agents Infiltrating Banks
record.summary: Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes has launched a criminal investigation into OpenAI and other AI companies over alleged infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents. The probe addresses concerns that sophisticated AI systems may have harmed banking infrastructure, with ongoing contact between the state and local banks.

record.title: Nigeria's Planned Biometric Air Travel System Raises Privacy and Exclusion Concerns
record.summary: Nigeria's government plans to mandate a biometric passenger verification system, requiring National Identification Numbers (NIN) for domestic flights from January 2027. The AI-driven system has sparked concerns over privacy, technical readiness, exclusion of foreigners and children, and potential travel disruptions, though no harm has yet occurred.

record.title: Chilean Army Captain Arrested for Possessing AI-Generated Child Sexual Abuse Material
record.summary: A 36-year-old Chilean Army captain was arrested in Puerto Aysén after authorities discovered over a thousand files of child sexual abuse material, some generated using AI, on his devices. The investigation revealed the use of AI tools to create highly realistic illegal content, leading to his detention and legal action.

record.title: South Korean Lawmaker Calls for Investigation into AI-Assisted Exam Cheating
record.summary: South Korean lawmaker Jeong Seong-guk has requested the preservation of university entrance exam materials to investigate suspicions of AI-assisted cheating using smart glasses and cameras. The call aims to verify if AI misuse undermined exam fairness, with potential for a broader probe if concrete evidence emerges. No confirmed incidents yet reported.

record.title: South Korea Preserves Exam Papers Amid AI Cheating Concerns
record.summary: South Korea's Prime Minister and Education Ministry ordered the preservation of last year's national college entrance exam papers due to rising concerns about potential AI-assisted cheating. The move aims to secure evidence for possible investigations, though no confirmed AI-related cheating incidents have occurred yet.

record.title: South Korean Civil Servant Uses ChatGPT to Forge Medical Certificates for Sick Leave
record.summary: A South Korean civil servant used ChatGPT to generate 41 fake medical certificates, submitting them to obtain 50 days of unauthorized sick leave and evade service duties. The individual was convicted of forgery and related offenses, receiving an eight-month suspended prison sentence. The incident highlights the misuse of generative AI for document forgery.

record.title: Suspect Arrested After Sharing Murder Plan with ChatGPT
record.summary: Israeli police arrested a northern resident after discovering he shared his plan to murder his wife with the AI chatbot ChatGPT. The suspect's communication with the AI system was pivotal in alerting authorities, leading to his arrest and the prevention of potential harm. The incident raises questions about AI privacy and law enforcement collaboration.

record.title: AI-Enabled Cheating Detected in South Korea's College Entrance Exam
record.summary: During South Korea's 2027 college entrance exam, 111 cases of cheating involving AI-powered smart devices, such as smart glasses and miniature cameras, were detected. Authorities used emergency disaster messages and AI-based detection methods to identify offenders, highlighting the growing misuse of AI in exam settings and its impact on fairness.

record.title: Singapore Central Bank Warns of AI Agents' Financial Risks, Plans Safeguards
record.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) warned that autonomous AI agents could rapidly move funds, posing liquidity and financial stability risks. MAS is developing a "Know Your Agent" protocol to verify AI agents' identities and authorities, aiming to mitigate potential harms as financial institutions adopt AI-driven transactions.

record.title: UN Warns of 'Medieval' AI Governance and Concentration of Power
record.summary: UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk warned at the RightsX summit in Geneva that AI governance is dangerously concentrated among a few tech companies, lacking democratic oversight and common regulations. He highlighted risks to human rights and critical infrastructure if AI development remains unchecked and unregulated.

record.title: AI-Enabled Cheating in South Korea's College Entrance Exam Spurs Whistleblower Program
record.summary: South Korea's Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission launched a two-month reporting period to combat cheating in the national college entrance exam using AI smart glasses and generative AI. Whistleblowers can receive up to 100 million KRW if their reports lead to administrative sanctions against offenders.

record.title: Anthropic Faces Criticism Over AI Safety Commitments Ahead of IPO
record.summary: A coalition of Nobel laureates, scientists, and tech leaders publicly challenged Anthropic's safety practices, accusing the company of weakening its safety commitments while racing to develop self-improving AI. The critics warn that such AI could escape human control, posing significant future risks. The event centers on Anthropic's US IPO.

record.title: SpaceXSI Denies Liability After Grok AI Generates Sexualised Images of UK Lawmaker
record.summary: Jess Asato, a UK lawmaker, sued SpaceXSI after its Grok AI platform generated non-consensual, sexualised images and videos of her. SpaceXSI denies liability, arguing such AI-generated content is obviously fictitious and not a privacy breach. The case tests legal responsibility for AI system design and misuse in the UK.

record.title: AI Chatbots and Social Media Linked to Child Harm in Canada
record.summary: Canadian experts report that AI chatbots and social media platforms have contributed to increased child suicide attempts, online bullying, and sexual trafficking. Pediatricians and child protection advocates highlight a surge in harm to children, urging swift passage of digital safety legislation to address these AI-driven risks.

record.title: AI-Generated Video Calls Used in Buzău Fraud Attempt
record.summary: A foreign suspect in Buzău, Romania, used AI-generated video calls to impersonate an official and deceive victims into believing their bank accounts were compromised. The scam, which aimed to steal over 140,000 lei, was thwarted by police, who arrested the perpetrator during the attempted money transfer.

record.title: Russian Use of Generative AI for Disinformation in Europe
record.summary: Russian special services are using generative AI to create and spread fake videos and disinformation, particularly in Central Europe. These AI-generated materials mimic reputable media and target elections and political figures, aiming to destabilize societies, foster division, and undermine political processes across European Union countries.

record.title: AI-Generated Fraudulent Websites Lead to Major Internet Scam Bust in Málaga
record.summary: Spanish police dismantled a Málaga-based criminal network that used AI to create fraudulent websites, enabling phishing and smishing attacks across Spain. The operation resulted in four arrests and the seizure of over €150,000 in assets. The AI-driven scams caused widespread financial and identity-related harm to victims.

record.title: AI-Driven Cyberattacks Escalate Threat to German Critical Infrastructure
record.summary: Germany faces a surge in cyberattacks, with AI systems enabling attackers to rapidly exploit vulnerabilities and disrupt critical infrastructure, such as supermarket and blood donation center cooling systems. The Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) reports a critical threat level, citing AI's role in automating and accelerating cyberattacks.

record.title: AI-Powered Cyberattack Targets EU Commission Personnel Systems
record.summary: In October, hackers used an AI model, reportedly of Chinese origin, to launch a cyberattack on the European Commission, targeting its personnel management systems. The attack led to operational disruptions, though no personal data theft was confirmed. The Commission responded by shutting down affected internal systems in Brussels.

record.title: Wisconsin Sues TikTok Over AI-Driven Addictive Features Harming Children
record.summary: Wisconsin has filed a lawsuit against TikTok, alleging its AI-powered recommendation system and addictive features intentionally target children, causing mental health harms such as anxiety, depression, and sleep disruption. The suit claims TikTok deceived parents about these risks, prioritizing profit over children's safety.

record.title: IEA Warns AI Datacentres to Drive 70% Rise in Carbon Emissions by 2030
record.summary: The International Energy Agency (IEA) warns that global datacentres, driven by rapid AI infrastructure expansion, will double their electricity consumption and generate 70% more carbon emissions by 2030. The US and China are leading this trend, primarily relying on fossil fuels to meet AI-related energy demands.

record.title: AI-Enabled Cheating in South Korean Tax Accountant Exam Spurs Class Action Lawsuit
record.summary: A top scorer in South Korea's 63rd tax accountant exam admitted to using generative AI, a miniature camera, and a smartphone to cheat. Law firm YK is organizing a class action lawsuit against the exam authority, citing failure to detect the AI-enabled cheating and resulting harm to other candidates.

record.title: Atiku Demands Audit and Transparency for INEC's Proposed AI Election System
record.summary: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress have called on Nigeria's electoral commission (INEC) to subject its proposed AI system for 2027 election result management to independent audit and public scrutiny, citing concerns that lack of transparency could undermine electoral integrity and public trust.
